name_structures.description: A Kirundi name is given first; a French Christian name is added later (often at baptism), and the original Kirundi name then works as the surname
name_structures.source: Duchaj, K. & Ntihirageza, J. (2009), York University (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md [B18]; RESEARCH_LOG.md, 26 Oct 2026); CENI Burundi, Élection des Députés 2025, liste nominative définitive des candidats, Province Bujumbura (https://www.ceniburundi.bi/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/BUJUMBURA-CANDIDATS-DEPUTES-2025.pdf), layout re-checked 9 Nov 2026: separate columns 'Nom' then 'Prénoms', both entirely in capitals; the file's ethnicity column was not read into any record and the download was deleted (DR-1.7): the Nom column holds Kirundi names and the Prénoms column French/Christian given names

name_structures.description: Before Christianisation there were no family names except for kings; missionaries imposed a hereditary patronymic system in which children bear their fathers' names
name_structures.source: University of Burundi repository, onomastics paper, §11.1.3, citing Bigangara (1982: 119) (https://repository.ub.edu.bi/bitstreams/c2369042-37ce-4c26-8692-fdefc04a65d1/download), read 5 Nov 2026; Simbananiye, L. (2005), Anthropologie et Sociétés 29(1): 167-181, p. 171: the traditional system, in which each person bears a name different from the father's, coexists with the patronymic system introduced by colonisation and Christianity; missionaries' attempt to impose the father's name 'fut un fiasco' (citing Rodegem 1965)

name_structures.description: Whether children share the father's name is disputed: the patronymic account above against the Rwanda-Rundi practice of a name chosen per child. The benchmark models it as the varied parameter p (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.2). Proximity to Rwanda is not evidence (CONCEPT-IDEA.md §2.3)
name_structures.source: Bigangara 1982 via University of Burundi (above), against Duchaj & Ntihirageza 2009; CONCEPT-IDEA.md §2.3; Simbananiye, L. (2005), 'Les noms de personnes au Burundi: un support du lien social', Anthropologie et Sociétés 29(1): 167-181 (https://www.erudit.org/fr/revues/as/2005-v29-n1-as993/011745ar.pdf), read in full 9 Nov 2026, p. 171: the traditional system, in which each person has a name different from the father's, 'cohabite avec le système patronymique introduit par la colonisation et le christianisme'; citing Rodegem (1965): missionaries' attempt to impose the father's name on children 'fut un fiasco'
name_structures.note: Simbananiye (2005) says both systems coexist, which supports keeping the varied parameter p rather than choosing one

name_structures.description: The name is obligatory and may be accompanied by one or more given names, which then form part of the name (art. 11). The name is the one on the birth record, or the one used constantly and publicly in childhood, at least up to age 16 (art. 12). It is given by whoever declares the birth, and its choice is free (art. 13); the registrar may object only if it could harm the child (art. 14). The law sets no inheritance of the father's name
name_structures.source: Burundi, Code des personnes et de la famille (1993), Titre II 'Du nom', arts 11-14 (http://jafbase.fr/docAfrique/Burundi/Burundi-Code-civil.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026; BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md [B4]

name_structures.description: Descent is expressed with mwene: 'Gahungu mwene Bucumi' = Gahungu, son of Bucumi. In a name given as 'X mwene Y', Y is the father's name and mwene is not part of either name
name_structures.source: Simbananiye, L. (2005), 'Les noms de personnes au Burundi: un support du lien social', Anthropologie et Sociétés 29(1): 167-181 (https://www.erudit.org/fr/revues/as/2005-v29-n1-as993/011745ar.pdf), read in full 9 Nov 2026, p. 171; Cox, E. E. (1969, rev. M. Philipps 2023), Kirundi-English dictionary (https://www.matana.de/kirundi.pdf), English-Kirundi part, read 9 Nov 2026: 'child (of) mwene', 'son (of) mwene'

name_structures.description: Some names are set by birth order or circumstance: Nyandwi, Minani, Nyawenda or Nyabenda, Bucumi (7th to 10th child), Karenzo (11th); twins Bukuru (elder) and Butoyi (younger); the child after twins Nkurikiye, Ciza or Congera. These names are common, so they distinguish people poorly; they are not, alone, evidence of birth order or kinship, and a father named Nyandwi cannot pass the name on meaningfully (one reason the patronymic system fits badly)
name_structures.source: Simbananiye, L. (2005), 'Les noms de personnes au Burundi: un support du lien social', Anthropologie et Sociétés 29(1): 167-181 (https://www.erudit.org/fr/revues/as/2005-v29-n1-as993/011745ar.pdf), read in full 9 Nov 2026, pp. 171-172; University of Burundi repository, 'Sociocultural prerequisites for understanding the Rundi nomenclature' (https://repository.ub.edu.bi/bitstreams/c2369042-37ce-4c26-8692-fdefc04a65d1/download; read 5 Nov 2026; server unreachable 9 Nov, passage confirmed from the search index): 'Nyandwi, the seventh child; Minani, the eighth child; Nyabenda, the ninth child'
name_structures.note: Two independent sources; they spell the ninth-child name differently (Nyawenda in Simbananiye 2005, Nyabenda in the University of Burundi paper), so the pair is recorded as variants

name_structures.description: Parents of twins are called by a title: Nyirababiri ('mother of twins') and Sebabiri ('father of twins'). A parent reported under such a title is being named by a status, not by a personal name
name_structures.source: Cox, E. E. (1969, rev. M. Philipps 2023), Kirundi-English dictionary (https://www.matana.de/kirundi.pdf), English-Kirundi part, read 9 Nov 2026: 'nyirababiri (ba-) mother of twins', 'sēbabiri (ba-) father of twins'

order_rules.description: Official candidate lists give the surname (Kirundi name) in a 'Nom' column before the given names in a 'Prénoms' column; both are written entirely in capitals, so capitals do not mark which element is the surname: the column does
order_rules.source: CENI Burundi, Élection des Députés 2025, liste nominative définitive des candidats, Province Bujumbura (https://www.ceniburundi.bi/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/BUJUMBURA-CANDIDATS-DEPUTES-2025.pdf), layout re-checked 9 Nov 2026: separate columns 'Nom' then 'Prénoms', both entirely in capitals; the file's ethnicity column was not read into any record and the download was deleted (DR-1.7)
order_rules.note: Corrected 9 Nov 2026: the earlier description (surname in capitals, given names in lower case: NSHIMIRIMANA Belyse) did not match the documents

order_rules.description: Aggregated name lists put Christian names in the surname slot ('Jean' as a surname), so order in foreign or scraped data is unreliable
order_rules.source: Forebears.io, Burundi surnames and forenames, observed 28 Oct 2026 (RESEARCH_LOG.md, G6 entry)

particles_and_morphemes.description: Names built on the root -hungu 'boy' (Gahungu, Buhungu) are boys' names. Used ONLY to keep generated names consistent with generated sex; never to infer anyone's sex (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md C12)
particles_and_morphemes.source: Cox, E. E. (1969, rev. M. Philipps 2023), Kirundi-English dictionary (https://www.matana.de/kirundi.pdf): umuhūngu 'boy, son', umukōbwa 'girl'; Simbananiye, L. (2005), Anthropologie et Sociétés 29(1): 167-181, p. 171: 'Le nom de Gahungu (petit garçon) ne peut être transmis à une fille'; profile bi-ceni-2026.1: noms containing -hungu seen 5+ times are all borne by men (9 of 9); pointer: University of Burundi study (2025) as reported by FunTimes Magazine (Gahungu/Buhungu boys, Gakobwa/Kigeme girls)

particles_and_morphemes.description: Names built on the root -kobwa 'girl' (Gakobwa) are girls' names. Same restriction: generation only, never inference
particles_and_morphemes.source: Cox, E. E. (1969, rev. M. Philipps 2023), Kirundi-English dictionary (https://www.matana.de/kirundi.pdf): umuhūngu 'boy, son', umukōbwa 'girl'; pointer: University of Burundi study (2025) as reported by FunTimes Magazine (Gahungu/Buhungu boys, Gakobwa/Kigeme girls)
particles_and_morphemes.note: The word meaning is certain (dictionary); its use in names comes from a second-hand report and no such name reached 5 occurrences in the CENI lists. Kigeme, also reported as a girls' name, has no primary source and is not included

transliteration_rules.description: Kinyarwanda cy is Kirundi c (cyane / cane). Deterministic in this direction only
transliteration_rules.source: Kinyarwanda and Kirundi Comparative Grammar (Dunwoody Press, 2007), §1.1.1, Table 1 (https://www.matana.de/kirundi_kinyarwanda.pdf)

transliteration_rules.description: Kinyarwanda shy is Kirundi sh (nshya / nsha)
Kinyarwanda by is Kirundi vy (umubyeyi / umuvyeyi; Habyarimana / Havyarimana)
transliteration_rules.source: Comparative Grammar (2007), Table 1; Forebears, Burundi surnames (Havyarimana ranked 25th, accessed 28 Oct 2026)

transliteration_rules.description: The reverse is not deterministic: both languages also have plain sh, c and j (ishami, igishanga). Going from Kirundi, generate both options, each as a hypothesis
Other Kirundi/Kinyarwanda differences are word by word (Rundi -anka / Rwanda -anga). They need sourced graph edges, not rules

Catholic (White Fathers) and Protestant (Alliance) mission spellings differ; the letter-level differences are not documented. The Protestant rules that can be read concern apostrophes, elision and word division (n'uko / nuko). Joined, split and apostrophe forms of a name are therefore treated as variants
transliteration_rules.source: Cox (1969, rev. Philipps 2023), Kirundi-English dictionary, orthography rules (https://www.matana.de/kirundi.pdf); Mioni (1975), J. Language Assoc. Eastern Africa 3(1): 21-26, abstract only; RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct 2026

phonetic_rules.description: [r] and [l] are one sound in Kirundi; a word or name may be written with either letter. Kirundi's own dictionary lists 'school' as ishūri, ishūli, ishure and ishule, and the Swahili loan kalamu became ikaramu ('pencil'). l survives mainly in foreign names (Luka, Yerusalemu in the Kirundi New Testament). Official place names show it too: the commune ISALE (CENI 2010) became Isare (Organic Law 1/05 of 16 March 2023)
phonetic_rules.source: Cox, E. E. (1969), Kirundi-English dictionary, rev. M. Philipps, Feb 2023, English-Kirundi part, entries 'school' and 'pencil' (https://www.matana.de/kirundi.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026; Kirundi New Testament, book list and text (dokumen.pub record, snippet only); IJLRHSS 3(3) for the shared Rwanda-Rundi phonology; CENI, Rapport général sur le processus électoral de 2010 (commune ISALE); Loi organique n°1/05 du 16 mars 2023, art. 5 (commune Isare)

phonetic_rules.description: Vowel length and tone are not written in ordinary spelling; linguistic texts mark them with circumflex, macron or caron. Search forms fold them; the original form is kept

Written consonant + w and consonant + y clusters are pronounced with a stop or nasal that the spelling does not show: tw [tkw], sw [skw], dw [dgw], bw [bg], pw [pk], fw [fk], mw [mŋ], nw [nŋw], rw [ɾgw] or, with the r dropped, [gw]; by/vy [vzɟ] (the vy of vyiza contains a z), my [mɲ]. Spelling follows the letters, speech does not
phonetic_rules.source: FSI, Kirundi Basic Course, pronunciation synopsis (based on Meeussen 1959) (https://fsi-languages.yojik.eu/languages/FSI/Kirundi/Basic/FSI%20-%20Kirundi%20Basic%20Course%20-%20Student%20Text.pdf); Nassenstein, Modern Africa (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct 2026); Kochetov, A. (2016), 'Palatalization and glide strengthening as competing repair strategies: evidence from Kirundi', Glossa 1(1): 14, 1-31 (https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.32), read in full 9 Nov 2026 (copy via the user): data from Ntihirageza (1993), Broselow & Niyondagara (1990) and Meeussen (1959), cross-checked with Cox (1969) and Rodegem (1970), confirmed with a Kirundi speaker from Bujumbura and by acoustic analysis (Kochetov et al. 2013), examples (4) and (28) and notes 4, 14
phonetic_rules.note: Raised 9 Nov 2026: Kochetov (2016) confirms each cluster with five earlier descriptions, a speaker and acoustic data. Correction: mw is [mŋ], not [my] as first recorded from the FSI synopsis

phonetic_rules.description: In some areas o becomes w before a and i in speech, but it is not written that way
phonetic_rules.source: Cox (1969, rev. 2023), orthography rules of the Alliance committee

phonetic_rules.description: Chichewa and Chitumbuka spelling has one accented letter, ŵ (standardised 1973). A Malawian writer may use it; search forms fold ŵ to w, and the original is kept
phonetic_rules.source: UK Government, Malawi Toponymic Factfile, 2025, 'Languages' (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/68aee2f02f1856648215588f/Malawi_Toponymic_Factfile.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026

phonetic_rules.description: Burundian speakers often say a French nasal vowel inside a word as an oral vowel plus a nasal consonant matching the next consonant (m before b/p, n before t/d, ŋ before k/g, ɱ before f/v), as in Kirundi prenasalised consonants: campagne [kampaɲ], cinquante [sɛŋkant], profonde [pʁɔfɔnd]. Word-internal 65.2% of nasal vowels; word-initial 26%; word-final 11.3% (the final nasal mostly stays). French ɑ̃ is fronted to [ã]. A French name said this way may be written by ear with an n or m: derived examples Vincent → Vinsent/Vinsenti, Ambroise → Ambrwaz
phonetic_rules.source: Nimbona, G. & Simon, A. C. (2022), 'La prononciation du français au Burundi: influence du français de Belgique et du kirundi', Journal of Language Contact 15: 481-511 (https://doi.org/10.1163/19552629-15030002), read in full 9 Nov 2026 (copy via the user), §5.1, Table 3 and examples
phonetic_rules.note: Corpus: 12 university-educated adults (mean age 38.5), mostly reading aloud; speakers born in Bujumbura were closest to standard French, and the authors attribute the differences to schooling, so less-schooled speakers and children may deviate more (not measured). Name examples marked 'derived' apply the pattern; they are not in the source

phonetic_rules.description: Two French vowels in a row are split with a glide: Louis [luwi] (10/12 speakers), mouette [muwɛt], lier [lije], million [milijɔ̃]; after a consonant + r/l, a j is inserted: étrier [etʁije] (11/12). French ui [ɥi] becomes [wi] or [y]: huit [wit] (12/12). Written by ear: Louis as Luwi; derived: Daniel as Danijel/Daniyeli, Gabriel as Gabriyeli
phonetic_rules.source: Nimbona, G. & Simon, A. C. (2022), 'La prononciation du français au Burundi: influence du français de Belgique et du kirundi', Journal of Language Contact 15: 481-511 (https://doi.org/10.1163/19552629-15030002), read in full 9 Nov 2026 (copy via the user), §5.3
phonetic_rules.note: Corpus: 12 university-educated adults (mean age 38.5), mostly reading aloud; speakers born in Bujumbura were closest to standard French, and the authors attribute the differences to schooling, so less-schooled speakers and children may deviate more (not measured). Name examples marked 'derived' apply the pattern; they are not in the source

phonetic_rules.description: French r is often dropped at the end of a word (the vowel before it is lengthened) and after a consonant: trois [twa] (7/12), quatre [kaːt] (7/12), pêcheur [peʃœː]; never at the start of a word. r also varies widely in sound (uvular, pharyngeal, Kirundi-style tap). Derived: Pierre heard as Pie/Pyè, Victoire as Viktwa
phonetic_rules.source: Nimbona, G. & Simon, A. C. (2022), 'La prononciation du français au Burundi: influence du français de Belgique et du kirundi', Journal of Language Contact 15: 481-511 (https://doi.org/10.1163/19552629-15030002), read in full 9 Nov 2026 (copy via the user), §5.2 and Table 5
phonetic_rules.note: Corpus: 12 university-educated adults (mean age 38.5), mostly reading aloud; speakers born in Bujumbura were closest to standard French, and the authors attribute the differences to schooling, so less-schooled speakers and children may deviate more (not measured). Name examples marked 'derived' apply the pattern; they are not in the source

phonetic_rules.description: French u [y] (absent from Kirundi) is occasionally said [u] or [i]: influence [ɛ̃fluwɑ̃s] (7/12), reliure [ʁəlijiʁ] (2/12); not general. Derived: Lucie heard as Lusi/Lusiya, Justine as Jistine
phonetic_rules.source: Nimbona, G. & Simon, A. C. (2022), 'La prononciation du français au Burundi: influence du français de Belgique et du kirundi', Journal of Language Contact 15: 481-511 (https://doi.org/10.1163/19552629-15030002), read in full 9 Nov 2026 (copy via the user), §5.1
phonetic_rules.note: Corpus: 12 university-educated adults (mean age 38.5), mostly reading aloud; speakers born in Bujumbura were closest to standard French, and the authors attribute the differences to schooling, so less-schooled speakers and children may deviate more (not measured). Name examples marked 'derived' apply the pattern; they are not in the source. Occasional only

phonetic_rules.description: Kirundi has h, French writes a silent h: about 1 speaker in 3 pronounced it (hasard [hazaʁ]). A French listener may drop an h the speaker said; derived: Hélène / Elène, Henri / Enri
phonetic_rules.source: Nimbona, G. & Simon, A. C. (2022), 'La prononciation du français au Burundi: influence du français de Belgique et du kirundi', Journal of Language Contact 15: 481-511 (https://doi.org/10.1163/19552629-15030002), read in full 9 Nov 2026 (copy via the user), §3.2 and §5.2
phonetic_rules.note: Corpus: 12 university-educated adults (mean age 38.5), mostly reading aloud; speakers born in Bujumbura were closest to standard French, and the authors attribute the differences to schooling, so less-schooled speakers and children may deviate more (not measured). Name examples marked 'derived' apply the pattern; they are not in the source

common_administrative_forms.description: Official lists write all name elements in capitals (CENI); case is kept in the source value and folded only in search forms. Capitals do not identify the surname in Burundian records
common_administrative_forms.source: CENI Burundi, Élection des Députés 2025, liste nominative définitive des candidats, Province Bujumbura (https://www.ceniburundi.bi/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/BUJUMBURA-CANDIDATS-DEPUTES-2025.pdf), layout re-checked 9 Nov 2026: separate columns 'Nom' then 'Prénoms', both entirely in capitals; the file's ethnicity column was not read into any record and the download was deleted (DR-1.7)

phoneme_inventory.note: accepted by all four Kirundi sources
phoneme_inventory.source: Comparative Grammar (2007), Table 27 (Meeussen 1959, Stevick 1965, Cristini 2000, Bennett 2001)

phoneme_inventory.note: one sound; Cristini (2000) lists it as dialectal
dialectal in Kirundi: accepted by Meeussen and Bennett, dialectal for Stevick, rejected by Cristini. Standard Kirundi writes c
one sound; accepted by all four sources
one sound; accepted by all four sources

phoneme_inventory.source: IJLRHSS 3(3); CONCEPT-IDEA.md §5.4A; Nimbona, G. & Simon, A. C. (2022), Journal of Language Contact 15: 481-511, §3.2: 'La consonne /l/ n'existe pas en kirundi' (ishule 'école' also said ishuri); prenasalised consonants are single units at the start of a syllable (/mb/ in Bujumbura, /nd/ in Burundi); Cox, E. E. (1969, rev. 2023), Kirundi-English dictionary: 'school: ishūri, ishūli, ishure, ishule' (bi-kirundi r-l-one-sound)

phoneme_inventory.note: each read as one unit; ng is not a separate phoneme for any Kirundi source
phoneme_inventory.source: Comparative Grammar (2007), ch. 2 and Table 27; Nimbona, G. & Simon, A. C. (2022), Journal of Language Contact 15: 481-511, §3.2: 'La consonne /l/ n'existe pas en kirundi' (ishule 'école' also said ishuri); prenasalised consonants are single units at the start of a syllable (/mb/ in Bujumbura, /nd/ in Burundi)

spelling_conventions.source: Cornevin, R. (1984), 'The standardization of the spelling of African names: toponyms and ethnonyms', in UNESCO, African ethnonyms and toponyms (General History of Africa: Studies and Documents 6), pp. 68-79 (https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000059805): French 'Adamaoua' for Adamawa, 'Haoussa' for Hausa/Hawsa, 'Tchouana' for Tswana; Official place names counted 9 Nov 2026 in places-2026.1 (DRC: HDX cod-ab-cod Référentiel Géographique Commun and older sources, 588 names; Burundi 149; Rwanda 48)
spelling_conventions.note: The spelling correspondence is part of French orthography (sources above); No ou, ch, tch, gn or dj in 149 official Burundian place names: French-style spellings appear only in colonial forms and in names written by French speakers

spelling_conventions.source: FSI, Introduction to French Phonology, Student Text (Salazar), p. 253, 'Pronunciation of written ch' (drills: chance, machine, chemin; the sound is taught by audio, not described in print) (https://fsi-languages.yojik.eu/languages/FSI/French/Fsi-FrenchPhonology-StudentText.pdf); Official place names counted 9 Nov 2026 in places-2026.1 (DRC: HDX cod-ab-cod Référentiel Géographique Commun and older sources, 588 names; Burundi 149; Rwanda 48)
spelling_conventions.note: The spelling correspondence is part of French orthography (sources above); Official Burundian names write sh (7: Gihosha, Kanyosha), never ch

spelling_conventions.source: FSI, Swahili Basic Course, Student Text, 'The Pronunciation of Swahili', pp. viii-xii (US Foreign Service Institute, public domain; https://fsi-languages.yojik.eu/languages/oldfsi/languages/Swahili/Basic/FSI%20-%20Swahili%20Basic%20Course%20-%20Student%20Text.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026

Cornevin, R. (1984), 'The standardization of the spelling of African names: toponyms and ethnonyms', in UNESCO, African ethnonyms and toponyms (General History of Africa: Studies and Documents 6), pp. 68-79 (https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000059805): French 'Tchouana' for Tswana (tch for an affricate); 'j and c(h) are usually given values close to their English value in anglophone countries, but not normally in francophone countries'; Official place names counted 9 Nov 2026 in places-2026.1 (DRC: HDX cod-ab-cod Référentiel Géographique Commun and older sources, 588 names; Burundi 149; Rwanda 48)
spelling_conventions.note: The spelling correspondence is part of French orthography (sources above); No tch or tsh in official Burundian names (they write c: Cibitoke, Cankuzo)

spelling_conventions.source: FSI, Swahili Basic Course, Student Text, 'The Pronunciation of Swahili', pp. viii-xii (US Foreign Service Institute, public domain; https://fsi-languages.yojik.eu/languages/oldfsi/languages/Swahili/Basic/FSI%20-%20Swahili%20Basic%20Course%20-%20Student%20Text.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026

spelling_conventions.note: a Kinyarwanda writer may write cy where Kirundi has c (reverse of rule rw-to-rn-cy). Orthographic correspondence stated in a published comparative grammar (Table 1)

spelling_conventions.source: FSI, Introduction to French Phonology, Student Text (Salazar), p. 254: 'When the consonant g is immediately followed by the vowels e or i it is always pronounced j' (https://fsi-languages.yojik.eu/languages/FSI/French/Fsi-FrenchPhonology-StudentText.pdf)

spelling_conventions.note: Swahili has no /ʒ/; its j is [dʒ], so a Swahili writer likely writes j
spelling_conventions.source: FSI, Swahili Basic Course, Student Text, 'The Pronunciation of Swahili', pp. viii-xii (US Foreign Service Institute, public domain; https://fsi-languages.yojik.eu/languages/oldfsi/languages/Swahili/Basic/FSI%20-%20Swahili%20Basic%20Course%20-%20Student%20Text.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026: sh is 'an unvoiced palatal grooved fricative (note the lack of a voiced counterpart)', so Swahili has no /ʒ/; j is 'as in English Joe'

FSI, Swahili Basic Course, p. xi: ny 'as in Spanish cañon, Portuguese nenhum, French gagner' (a palatal nasal), so French writes the sound gn; Official place names counted 9 Nov 2026 in places-2026.1 (DRC: HDX cod-ab-cod Référentiel Géographique Commun and older sources, 588 names; Burundi 149; Rwanda 48)
spelling_conventions.note: The spelling correspondence is part of French orthography (sources above); gn appears in none of 785 official place names of the three countries (ny: 33); a French writer by ear may still write gn

spelling_conventions.source: FSI, Swahili Basic Course, Student Text, 'The Pronunciation of Swahili', pp. viii-xii (US Foreign Service Institute, public domain; https://fsi-languages.yojik.eu/languages/oldfsi/languages/Swahili/Basic/FSI%20-%20Swahili%20Basic%20Course%20-%20Student%20Text.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026
spelling_conventions.note: written ny before vowels, n before consonants (nchi)

spellings: l after a, o or u
l at the start of a word (no Chichewa word begins with r)
r for l after i or e (hypercorrection)
spelling_conventions.note: Sourced: the writing rule (Chirwa 2008, from the Chichewa Orthography Rules; 1973 date from the UK factfile). Hypothesis, not sourced: that Malawian clerks apply it to refugees' names (word-initial l: Rukundo as Lukundo; after a/o/u: Nkurunziza as Nkulunziza; hypercorrect r after i/e)
spelling_conventions.source: Chirwa, M. N. (2008), 'Trill maintenance and replacement in Chichewa: a study on newsreaders' speech from three radio stations in Malawi', MA dissertation, University of Cape Town (http://hdl.handle.net/11427/10191), read 9 Nov 2026: pp. 4-5 and 31, citing Mchombo (2001) and the Chichewa Orthography Rules: [r] and [l] are allophones of one phoneme; <r> is written after the front vowels i and e, <l> after a, o and u, within a morpheme; no Chichewa word begins with r; in speech the trill is often replaced by [l], and writers unsure of the rule hypercorrect (ndili misspelled ndiri); UK Government, Malawi Toponymic Factfile (2025), 'Languages' (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/68aee2f02f1856648215588f/Malawi_Toponymic_Factfile.pdf): 'The orthography of Chichewa was standardised in 1973 in the New Chichewa Orthography Rules'

spelling_conventions.note: Chichewa Board spelling writes ch (and tch when aspirated), never c alone, so a Malawian clerk may write a c-name as ch (Ciza as Chiza); that clerks do so with refugees' names is a hypothesis
spelling_conventions.source: Peace Corps Malawi, 'An Introduction to the Chichewa Language' ('The letter C always carries an H'; no Q or X) (https://files.peacecorps.gov/multimedia/audio/languagelessons/malawi/MW_Chichewa_Language_Lessons.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026; Downing, L. J. & Mtenje, A. (2017), The Phonology of Chichewa, Oxford University Press, ch. 1, note 2 (publisher preview, https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9780191037733_A30389705/preview-9780191037733_A30389705.pdf), read 9 Nov 2026: the Chichewa Board's convention writes the unaspirated affricate as ch and the aspirated one as tch; earlier work (Watkins 1937) and some linguists write c

relationship_implications.note: If the patronymic practice applies (p), shared surnames among a father's children are expected and disagreement counts against kinship; if names are chosen per child, disagreement is neutral. Which practice applies is not known per family

known_failure_modes.description: A Burundian name written in Kinyarwanda spelling (Havyarimana as Habyarimana) by a Rwandan clerk or in Rwandan records; see transliteration_rules
The Kirundi name and the Christian name swap places: order in CENI lists is surname first, in foreign systems often given name first, and aggregators put Christian names in the surname slot
The French Christian name changes form with the writer's language (Jean / John / Yohana); handled by the cross-pack given-name data (week 4)
Joined, split and apostrophe forms of the same name (mission spelling habits); see mission-spellings
Names written by a clerk who hears the spoken form follow the sounds, not the spelling; see listener_confusions

Burundian refugees in Tanzanian towns took Swahili names to be less visible, and some kept them after naturalisation. Such a name is not a spelling variant and gets no public edge; matching across it goes through the protected route
known_failure_modes.source: Daley (2018), Oxford (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md [B18]); NAME_CHANGE.md rules 1 and 5; THREAT_MODEL.md T14

known_failure_modes.description: Places renamed or respelled after independence: Kitega / Gitega, Usumbura / Bujumbura (1962), Hinga or Muhinga / Muyinga, Karusi / Karuzi. Older people may give the old form; foreign records may keep it. Goes into the cross-pack place data (week 4)
known_failure_modes.source: Statoids, Burundi provinces, 'Other names of subdivisions' and history (https://statoids.com/ubi.html); accessed 5 Nov 2026; Niyonkuru, L. (1987), 'Loan-words in Kirundi: a preliminary study', African Study Monographs 7: 81-87, pp. 82-83 (Usumbura as the Swahili rendering of Bujumbura)

known_failure_modes.description: Swahili renders Kirundi class prefixes differently (Burundi as Urundi, Barundi/Abarundi as Warundi): a name or place given through Swahili may carry a different prefix. Places too: Usumbura for Bujumbura, Uzige for Buzige
known_failure_modes.source: Alexandre, P. (1984), in UNESCO, African ethnonyms and toponyms, p. 65: "'Urundi' and 'Warundi' are Swahili for 'Burundi' and 'Barundi/Abarundi'"; Niyonkuru, L. (1987), 'Loan-words in Kirundi: a preliminary study', African Study Monographs 7: 81-87 (Kyoto University; copy via the user, read in full 9 Nov 2026), pp. 82-83: 'Usumbura - Swahili rendition for Bujumbura'; 'Urundi (Kiswahili for Burundi)'; 'Uzige - or Buzige in Kirundi'

known_failure_modes.description: Country of origin does not fix the naming language. Burundi has long-settled Kinyarwanda-speaking communities (refugees of 1959-64 and 1972-73, in Bujumbura, Bubanza, Muyinga, Ruyigi) and Swahili-speaking communities from eastern Congo in Bujumbura and the Rusizi plain; a person from Burundi may carry names spelled by Kinyarwanda or Swahili conventions. Try the rw-kiny and cd-swc-ln packs as well as bi-kirundi
known_failure_modes.source: Niyonkuru, L. (1987), 'Loan-words in Kirundi: a preliminary study', African Study Monographs 7: 81-87 (Kyoto University; copy via the user, read in full 9 Nov 2026), pp. 81-82 and 84: Kinyarwanda speakers arrived as refugees in 1959-1964 and 1972-1973 (Bujumbura, Bubanza, Muyinga, Ruyigi); 'Congolese' were 57.3% of the urban and semi-urban population of Usumbura in the 1950s and spoke Kingwana (Congo Swahili); immigrant groups from eastern Zaire along Lake Tanganyika and the Rusizi valley. Group names in the source are not carried into the pack (DR-1.7)

known_failure_modes.description: 'X mwene Y' parsed as a three-part name. Split on mwene: X is the person, Y the father

Some real names mean 'nothing' or 'without a name' (Ntazina 'no name', Busabusa 'nothing', Ntakije 'nothing comes'), given to hide a child from misfortune. They must not be treated as a missing or placeholder name
known_failure_modes.source: Simbananiye, L. (2005), 'Les noms de personnes au Burundi: un support du lien social', Anthropologie et Sociétés 29(1): 167-181 (https://www.erudit.org/fr/revues/as/2005-v29-n1-as993/011745ar.pdf), read in full 9 Nov 2026, p. 171

known_failure_modes.description: A parent reported as Nyirababiri or Sebabiri (mother/father of twins) is named by a title shared by every parent of twins; it must not be matched as a personal name
